about.title: Tustin Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription:
Something felt wrong after a procedure, a diagnosis came too late, or a medication was given at the wrong dose. If that happened to you or a family member in Tustin, you are probably carrying more questions than answers. We are here to help: our team reviews medical malpractice cases in Orange County and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless we recover for you.

Medical malpractice cases in California run on their own rules. Under MICRA, you generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit begins. Nearly every claim also depends on a qualified medical expert explaining what the standard of care required and how it was missed. A poor result by itself is not malpractice; we can help sort out where your experience falls.

items.title: MICRA deadlines are unforgiving
items.desc: California allows one year from discovery and no more than three years from the injury, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice. Getting in touch early gives us room to work within those windows.

items.title: Expert review comes first
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always required before a claim can move forward. We know how to arrange that review and what it needs to show.

items.title: Free to you, contingency for us
items.desc: We charge nothing for a case review, and we are paid only if we recover for you. You can find out whether you have a case without spending money to ask.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Red Hill Avenue and then my emergency care made things worse. Is that one claim or two?
items.answer: It may be two separate matters with two separate sets of rules. The crash itself falls under ordinary personal injury law, while mistakes in the treatment that followed are governed by MICRA, with its own deadlines and expert requirement. We can review both parts and explain how they fit together.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: MICRA places a cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, and that cap rises each year. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are treated differently. We can explain how the current figures apply to your circumstances without predicting any particular result.

items.question: My surgery had a bad outcome. Does that automatically mean malpractice?
items.answer: No. A disappointing or even serious result can happen when care was entirely appropriate. Malpractice means the provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that failure caused the harm. Sorting the two apart is exactly what a qualified medical expert and our team do together.
